gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-quicksand: Quicksand stands tall and round, its bowls like blown glass bulbs. Arkhip floats its geometric letters far apart up top, and the uniform bars below carry that same lightness down the page.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-almendra-sc: Modern, geometric Arkhip holds a ruler-straight line weight, its letters floating well apart. Almendra SC adds a dignified text serif voice, its mouths staying open, against that rigid heading line.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-antic-slab: Not a trace of stroke modulation marks Arkhip, with its letters floating well apart. Antic Slab follows with dignified, editorial letters and round bowls whose walls never bulge anywhere.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-biorhyme: BioRhyme reads bookish and refined, with widely spaced capitals. Across a full column its curve ends stop like lifted brush strokes, a soft contrast to Arkhip's flat, unmodulated heading letters.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-biz-udmincho: BIZ UDMincho reads bookish and traditional, with a shallow terminal curl and a wide gap. But Arkhip's tube-like strokes look like neon glass beside it, with letters floating well apart.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-copse: Tube-like thickness that holds through every bend defines Arkhip, a modern display face. Copse, a literary text serif, takes over for reading, with daylight visible through each curved opening.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-cutive: Refined, literary Cutive runs with wide tracking. Arkhip does its best work as a modern, uniform-stroke display line, while Cutive handles the running text with an open c.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-david-libre: Modern geometry up top, then dignified David Libre below it. Arkhip builds every letter from one stroke width, while the serif's terminals hang open, giving the text a refined softness.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-gentium-plus: Gentium Plus opens each c like a pitcher's wide mouth, classic and refined. Gentium Plus is built for reading, whereas Arkhip's constant-width strokes, like bent pipe, are made for display.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-inika: A single constant stroke width defines Arkhip, a modern display face with letters floating apart. And it earns its keep big and short, while Inika, a traditional text serif, lets you see through each s.
